note.explanation: The Arrhenius idea classifies acids and bases by what they produce when they dissociate in water. An acid produces H⁺ or H₃O⁺, while a base produces OH⁻. The amount of ionization also helps us describe an acid or base as strong or weak.
examples: HCl ionizes in water to form H₃O⁺ and Cl⁻.
NaOH ionizes in water to form Na⁺ and OH⁻.
note.checkAnswer: NaOH is an Arrhenius base because it dissociates in water to give OH⁻ ions.
note.simple: In water, acids give H₃O⁺ and bases give OH⁻. Strong substances ionize more completely; weak substances ionize only partly.
note.checkQuestion: Why is NaOH an Arrhenius base?
note.title: Arrhenius Acids and Bases
steps: An acid is that substance which dissociates in water to give proton (H⁺) or hydronium ion (H₃O⁺).
A base is that substance which dissociates in water to give hydroxyl ions (OH⁻).
For example: HCl(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq).
Acid strength depends upon the extent to which it is ionized in water.
note.answer: Arrhenius acids produce H⁺ or H₃O⁺ in water; Arrhenius bases produce OH⁻ in water.

mcqs.stem: According to the Arrhenius concept, which ion is produced when an acid dissociates in water?
rationales: Correct: the Arrhenius definition says an acid gives H⁺ or H₃O⁺ in water.
Cl⁻ is the chloride ion and is not the acid-producing ion in this definition.
Na⁺ is a positive ion produced by some bases, such as NaOH.
OH⁻ is the ion produced by an Arrhenius base.

mcqs.stem: Which substance is an Arrhenius base?
rationales: HNO₃ is an Arrhenius acid because it produces hydronium ions in water.

H₂SO₄ is an Arrhenius acid because it produces hydronium ions in water.

mcqs.stem: Which equation shows the neutralization step described by the Arrhenius concept?
rationales: Correct: hydronium and hydroxyl ions react to form water and release heat.
The textbook describes Na⁺ and Cl⁻ as hydrated spectator ions in solution, not as solid NaCl crystals forming there.
This equation does not represent the neutralization products.
This equation is not the reaction between hydronium and hydroxyl ions.

mcqs.stem: Which acid is described in this section as ionizing only to a very limited extent?
rationales: H₂SO₄ is described as a mineral acid that ionizes in two steps.
HNO₃ is described as a mineral acid that ionizes in a single step.
Correct: acetic acid is an organic acid and is described as ionizing to a very limited extent.
HCl is described as ionizing completely in water.

rationales: NaOH is given as an example of a strong base.
KOH is given as an example of a strong base.
Ba(OH)₂ is listed as a typical Arrhenius base, not as a weak base example in this section.
Correct: NH₄OH is given as a weak base because it only partially ionizes in water.

options: It is completely converted into Na⁺ and OH⁻.
It does not dissolve in water.
mcqs.stem: Which statement describes the ionization of NaOH in water?
rationales: Correct: NaOH is a strong base and ionizes completely in water to form Na⁺ and OH⁻.
The section identifies NaOH as a base that ionizes in water, not as an insoluble substance.
NaOH is described as ionizing completely, not remaining undissociated.
Producing H₃O⁺ is the Arrhenius behaviour of an acid, not NaOH.

written.text: Q7.5. What is the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid?
written.finalAnswer: A strong acid ionizes to a large extent in water; a concentrated acid contains a large amount of acid in a given volume of solution.

rubric.why: The distinction depends on ionization for acid strength.
rubric.description: States that strength concerns the extent of ionization.
rubric.how: Explain that a strong acid ionizes to a large extent in water.

rubric.why: Concentration describes how much acid is present in a solution.
rubric.description: States that concentration concerns the amount of acid.
rubric.how: Mention the amount of acid in a given volume of solution.

rubric.why: A clear contrast between the two terms is needed for a complete answer.
rubric.how: Keep extent of ionization separate from amount of dissolved acid.

modelAnswer: A strong acid ionizes to a large extent in water.
A concentrated acid contains a large amount of acid in a given volume of solution.
Therefore, strength depends on ionization, whereas concentration depends on the amount of acid present.
A strong acid is not necessarily concentrated, and a concentrated acid is not necessarily strong.

written.text: Q7.1. Acids play significant roles within human body. Comment on this statement.
written.finalAnswer: The stomach produces hydrochloric acid to digest food. If more acid is produced than required, stomach acidity can result; weak bases such as calcium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide in antacids neutralize the excess acid.

rubric.why: The section identifies stomach hydrochloric acid as an important body acid.
rubric.description: Names the acid produced by the stomach.
rubric.how: State that the stomach produces hydrochloric acid.

rubric.why: The answer must explain the useful role of the stomach acid.
rubric.how: Explain that hydrochloric acid helps digest food.

rubric.why: The section also explains that excessive acid causes a problem.
rubric.how: Mention that producing more acid than needed can cause stomach acidity.

rubric.why: This links the acid's effect to the treatment described in the text.
rubric.how: State that antacids neutralize stomach acid.

rubric.why: Examples from the section support the explanation.
rubric.description: Names the weak bases used in antacids.
rubric.how: Give calcium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide as examples.

modelAnswer: The stomach produces hydrochloric acid to digest the food that we eat.
If stomach cells produce more acid than the stomach needs, the person suffers from stomach acidity.
Weak bases such as calcium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide are used as antacids.
These antacids neutralize the stomach acid.
Thus, acids have an important role in digestion, but excess acid can cause discomfort.

explain.title: Arrhenius acids
explain.body: An acid is that substance which dissociates in water to give proton (H⁺) or hydronium ion (H₃O⁺). For example, HCl ionizes in water to form H₃O⁺ and Cl⁻.

explain.title: Arrhenius bases
explain.body: A base is that substance which dissociates in water to give hydroxyl ions (OH⁻). For example, NaOH gives Na⁺ and OH⁻ in water.

explain.title: Water and neutralization
explain.body: Water surrounds the ions formed in solution. In a strong acid–strong base neutralization, H₃O⁺ and OH⁻ react to form water and release heat: H₃O⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → 2H₂O(l) + Heat.

explain.title: Strong and weak ionization
explain.body: The strength of an acid depends upon the extent to which it is ionized in water. Mineral acids such as HCl ionize extensively, while organic acids such as acetic acid ionize to a very limited extent. NaOH and KOH are strong bases; NH₄OH is a weak base that only partially ionizes.

explain.title: Acids in the stomach
explain.body: The stomach produces hydrochloric acid to digest food. Too much acid can cause stomach acidity. Weak bases such as calcium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide are used in antacids to neutralize stomach acid.

mistakes: Writing OH⁻ as the ion produced by an Arrhenius acid; acids produce H⁺ or H₃O⁺.
Writing H₃O⁺ as the ion produced by an Arrhenius base; bases produce OH⁻.
Confusing acid strength with concentration: strength concerns ionization, while concentration concerns the amount of acid in solution.
Forgetting the charges on ions when writing ionization equations.
Saying that NaCl forms as solid crystals during neutralization in water; the textbook describes hydrated Na⁺ and Cl⁻ spectator ions in solution.
